What can we do to get ready? (Pray, say sorry, be kind, share.)
practice: Give each child a paper with 24 or 25 small boxes (or a wreath-shaped calendar).
In each box, write or draw an act of love, such as: “Hug someone,” “Pray for a friend,” “Help set the table,” “Share a toy,” “Write a thank-you note.”
Let children decorate it with stickers and colors.
Take it home and open a box every day of Advent.
script.close: Light an Advent candle. Pray: “Come, Lord Jesus.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Do one act of love each day.”

tryit: Make an Advent calendar with acts of love.
lessons.saintStory:
Mary and Joseph were an ordinary young couple in Nazareth, engaged to be married. When the angel told Mary that God had chosen her to be the mother of Jesus, she said yes. Joseph was told in a dream not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife.
They prepared for the baby. Then the emperor ordered a census, and they had to travel to Bethlehem, about ninety miles, with Mary expecting. When they arrived, there was no room at the inn. Joseph found a place for them in a stable. There Jesus was born, and Mary wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger.
Mary and Joseph show us how to wait for Jesus: with trust, with love, and with open hearts.

lessons.title: Lent and Easter
lessons.idea: In Lent we pray, fast and give. At Easter we celebrate that Jesus is alive.
lessons.question: What can we give up or share?
lessons.activity: Choose a small Lenten promise.
teach: In Lent we pray, fast and give (Matthew 6:1–18; CCC 538, 1438). Easter celebrates that Jesus is alive (CCC 1169).
Choose a small promise.
Easter lasts fifty days.
quiz: Lent lasts…|Seven days|Ten days|Forty days|One month|2|CCC 540.
During Lent we…|Party|Forget|Travel|Pray, fast, give|3|Matthew 6.
Easter celebrates…|The Resurrection|Pentecost|The birth|The ascension|0|CCC 638.
lessons.life: Choose a Lenten promise and tell your family.
lessons.saint: Thomas the Apostle: he doubted at first, and then said, “My Lord and my God!”
lessons.mem: Jesus is risen, alleluia!
lessons.hook: Show ashes and a candle. “Lent and Easter.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What is your Lenten promise?”

script.open: Bring a plain, dried branch and a vase of flowers. Say, “In Lent, a church is quiet, like this branch. At Easter, it bursts into flowers, with joy. Today we will see why.”
teach: Say: “Lent is the forty days before Easter. In Lent we get ready to celebrate that Jesus is alive. We do three things: we pray, we fast and we give to the poor. Jesus talked about them in Matthew 6: ‘When you give to the needy,’ ‘when you pray,’ ‘when you fast.’ And he told us to do them quietly, for God and not to be noticed.”

Say: “To pray means to talk to God more. To fast means to give up something good, to remind us of God, like candy or a game, or eating less. To give means to share with the poor. On Ash Wednesday we receive ashes on our foreheads, a sign that we are sorry and want to turn back to God. On Fridays in Lent, we do not eat meat.”

Say: “Then comes Holy Week. On Palm Sunday, Jesus enters Jerusalem. On Holy Thursday, he gives us the Eucharist. On Good Friday, he dies on the cross. And on Easter Sunday, he rises! The whole Church sings ‘Alleluia.’ Lent leads to Easter joy.”
ask: What are the three things we do in Lent? (Pray, fast and give.)
What do we receive on Ash Wednesday? (Ashes.)
What happened on Easter? (Jesus rose from the dead.)
practice: Give each child a card and crayons. Say: “Choose one small promise for Lent: to pray each night, to give up a treat, to help at home, or to put a coin in a box for the poor.”
Write it, decorate it, and sign it.
Put the card where you will see it, such as the fridge.
Say together: “Jesus is risen, alleluia!” with joy.
script.close: Pray: “Jesus, help me keep my Lenten promise.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Tell your family your promise and keep it.”

lessons.saintStory:
Thomas was one of the twelve apostles. When Jesus said he was going to Bethany, where his friend Lazarus had died, and it was dangerous, Thomas said to the others, “Let us also go, that we may die with him.” He was brave and loyal.
But on the evening of the first Easter, Thomas was not with the others when Jesus appeared to them. When they told him, he said, “Unless I see the marks of the nails in his hands, I will not believe.” A week later Jesus came again, and said to Thomas, “Put your finger here. See my hands. Do not doubt, but believe.” Thomas answered, “My Lord and my God!”
Tradition says that Thomas later traveled all the way to India to tell people about Jesus. He shows us what Easter faith is: seeing that Jesus is truly alive, and believing.

lessons.title: Holy days and feasts
lessons.idea: We celebrate feasts of Mary and the saints and holy days like All Saints.
lessons.question: What is your favorite feast?
lessons.activity: Mark your family’s feast days on a calendar.
teach: Feast days celebrate Mary, the saints and mysteries (CCC 1172, 2043). All Saints Nov. 1; All Souls Nov. 2.
Mark your family’s feast days.
Revelation 7:9: a great multitude.
talk: How can we celebrate at home?
quiz: All Saints is on…|December 25|January 1|Easter|November 1|3|Liturgy.
All Souls is for…|The kids|The saints|The dead|The angels|2|CCC 1032.
Holy days of obligation need…|Silence|Parties|Mass|School|2|CCC 2180.
lessons.life: Celebrate a saint’s feast day with a story and a treat.
lessons.saint: All the saints: they show many ways to love God.
lessons.mem: Holy ones of God, pray for us.
lessons.hook: Show a calendar with feast days. “Today is a feast of…”
lessons.assess: Ask children to name a feast day and its meaning.

script.open: Hold up a calendar and say, “Look at all these days. Some are birthdays, some are holidays. The Church has special days for celebrating, too. They are called feast days. What do you think a feast day is?”
teach: Say: “A feast day is a day when the Church celebrates something special. There are feasts of Jesus, like Christmas and Easter. There are feasts of Mary, like the Immaculate Conception on December 8, and the Assumption on August 15. And there are feasts of saints. Each saint has a day. For example, St. Nicholas is December 6, and St. Patrick is March 17.”

Say: “Some feasts are holy days of obligation, special days when Catholics go to Mass, like Christmas and All Saints. And on All Saints’ Day, November 1, we remember all the saints, including those who aren’t named. Revelation 7 describes a huge crowd in heaven, too many to count. We are part of that family.”

Say: “We can celebrate feasts at home too. We can bake a cake or have a special dinner, or read the saint’s story. Your family’s feast days might include birthdays, baptism days and the feast of your patron saint. They remind us that God’s friends are our friends.”
ask: What is a feast day? (A special day to celebrate Jesus, Mary or a saint.)

lessons.saintStory:
On November 1 the Church celebrates All Saints’ Day. This feast started about 1,300 years ago, when a Roman pope turned an old temple, the Pantheon, into a church to honor Mary and all the martyrs. Soon the whole Church was keeping a day for all the saints.
The book of Revelation describes a great crowd in heaven, too many to count, from every nation, wearing white robes and praising God. They are the saints. The next day, November 2, is All Souls’ Day, when we pray for those who have died and are being made ready for heaven.
There are saints we know by name and many more we do not know. They are mothers, fathers, children, farmers, teachers, soldiers, kings. All Saints’ Day tells us that every one of us is called to be a saint.
